insights: energy.csv is a single 19,735-row, 10-minute smart-house panel with no missing values; Appliances is a numeric Wh target with median 60, mean 97.7, and max 1080, suggesting right-skewed consumption that tree models can handle.
rv1 and rv2 have identical summary statistics and 19,735 unique values, consistent with random control columns; they should be excluded as non-informative noise.
lights, T_out, Press_mm_hg, RH_out, Windspeed, Visibility, and Tdewpoint are excluded because the objective restricts inputs to T1..T9/RH_1..RH_9 and calendar information.
A temporal holdout on date is appropriate because the virtual meter must estimate the same interval from contemporaneous sensors and future intervals must not leak into training.

Evening 17-22 underestimation is best monitored as a diagnostic residual bias by hour; adding hour and is_evening_17_22 features may help the model learn time-of-day patterns without changing the primary RMSE objective.
This is a single-house estimation task; results should not be interpreted as transferable to new buildings.
questions: Should evening 17-22 performance be a separate diagnostic, a weighted RMSE, or a hard constraint on underestimation?
Is Appliances the intended appliance-only target, or should lights be subtracted if the Appliances column includes lights?
Are T6 and RH_6 intended as indoor/building sensors, or should they be excluded if they represent outdoor conditions?
preparation: Use energy.csv as a single table with no joins. Parse date as datetime for temporal splitting and derive calendar features: hour, dayofweek, month, is_weekend, and is_evening_17_22. Target is Appliances. Exclude raw date, lights, T_out, Press_mm_hg, RH_out, Windspeed, Visibility, Tdewpoint, rv1, and rv2. Features are the 18 allowed sensor columns T1, RH_1, T2, RH_2, T3, RH_3, T4, RH_4, T5, RH_5, T6, RH_6, T7, RH_7, T8, RH_8, T9, RH_9 plus the derived calendar features. Use standard preprocessing and a temporal holdout on date; evaluate overall RMSE and diagnostic residual bias for hours 17-22.
rationale: Appliances is a defensible same-interval regression target for a virtual meter. The allowed inputs are contemporaneous room/building sensors and calendar features, so no lag or future-weather features are needed. A temporal split prevents leakage from future intervals. RMSE matches the stated overall error objective, while hour and is_evening_17_22 support diagnosing evening underestimation. Linear, random forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost provide a low-capacity control plus nonlinear CPU tabular models suitable for skewed, sensor-driven consumption.
